step1_analysis.description: A cascaded two-stage common-source amplifier using NMOS transistors. It represents a single-ended half-circuit of the cascaded differential pairs mentioned in the paper, forming the core of a broadband amplifier (though inductive peaking components are omitted in this simplified netlist).

paper_reference.title: 40-Gb/s Amplifier and ESD Protection Circuit in 0.18-m CMOS Technology

Voltage Gain.description: Low-frequency or midband voltage gain of the cascaded amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming VDD=1.8V, VIN_DC=0.7V. Stage 1: Id1~105uA, gm1~0.75mA/V, R1=5k -> Gain1 = 3.75. Stage 2: Id2~975uA, gm2~2.3mA/V, R2=800 -> Gain2 = 1.84. Total Gain = 3.75 * 1.84 = 6.9 V/V = 16.7 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on the chosen load resistors (5k and 800 ohms) added to the testbench to keep both stages in saturation with a 0.7V DC input, matching the paper's reported gain.

Unity Gain Bandwidth.description: Frequency at which the voltage gain drops to 0 dB (unity).

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominant pole at interstage node X: R1=5k, Cx~30fF (Cgd1 + Cdb1 + Cgs2 + Miller) -> fp1 ~ 1 GHz. UGBW = Gain * fp1 ~ 6.9 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 0.5um channel length in the extracted netlist and the lack of inductive peaking (T-coils) significantly reduce the bandwidth compared to the paper's 40Gb/s highly-optimized design.

Power Consumption.description: Total DC power dissipation of the two amplifier stages.

sky130_expected.calculation: Id1 = 105uA, Id2 = 975uA. Total current = 1.08mA. Power = 1.08mA * 1.8V = 1.94 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The extracted netlist only contains two core transistors. The 190 mW reported in the paper includes the entire multi-stage differential amplifier chain and 50-ohm output drivers.

Transient Output Swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output for a given input signal.

sky130_expected.calculation: Input is 10mV amplitude (20mVpp). Expected output = 20mVpp * 6.9 (linear gain) = 138 mVpp.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Verifies large-signal time-domain amplification matches the small-signal AC gain.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure AC gain, unity gain bandwidth, transient output swing, and DC power consumption of the two-stage amplifier. Load resistors are added to establish proper DC biasing and gain.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Two-Stage Common-Source Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

XM1 X VIN GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 LABEL_NET_1 X GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Biasing and Loads
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVIN VIN 0 DC 0.7 AC 1 SIN(0.7 0.01 100MEG 0 0)

* Load resistors to convert the bare transistors into an amplifier
R1 VDD X 5k
R2 VDD LABEL_NET_1 800

* Analyses
.control
  * DC Operating Point and Power
  op
  let total_current = -i(VVDD)
  let power = total_current * 1.8
  print power
  print v(X) v(LABEL_NET_1)

  * AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
  ac dec 100 1MEG 100G
  let gain_db = vdb(LABEL_NET_1)
  meas ac gain_1mhz find gain_db at=1MEG
  meas ac ugbw when gain_db=0 fall=1

  * Transient Analysis for Output Swing
  tran 0.1n 50n
  meas tran vout_pp pp v(LABEL_NET_1)
  
  quit
.endc
.end
